sentences.cn_text: 无线电的先驱们将其视为献给全人类的礼物。
sentences.en_text: The pioneers of wireless saw it as a gift to all the people.

sentences.cn_text: 约翰·里斯爵士说它将终结「精神上的孤立」，并欣喜地表示：「无论有多少千人在收听，总有足够的空间容纳他人……天才与愚者、富人与穷人同时聆听。」
sentences.en_text: Sir John Reith said that it would end “isolation of the spirit” and rejoiced: “It does not matter how many thousands may be listening, there is always enough for others...the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously.”

sentences.cn_text: 在两次世界大战之间，这项技术革新催生了一种新的国家意识。
sentences.en_text: Between two great wars this technological innovation built a new kind of national consciousness.

sentences.cn_text: 本周开幕，由比蒂·鲁本斯在牛津大学博德利图书馆策划的一本书和一场展览，记录了无线电如何在1922年至1939年间改变日常生活。
sentences.en_text: Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939.

sentences.cn_text: 她援引了书信、日记和小说，以及温妮弗雷德·吉尔1939年的一份逐字记录的受众研究田野笔记。
sentences.en_text: She draws on letters, diaries and fiction, and a 1939 field notebook of verbatim audience research by Winifred Gill.

sentences.cn_text: 人们享受纯粹新奇感的证言中不乏趣味。
sentences.en_text: There’s fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness.

sentences.cn_text: 一幅漫画讽刺了一群人无法交谈，因为他们都戴着耳机。
sentences.en_text: A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they’re all in headphones.

sentences.cn_text: 有人称广播音乐让工人们哼唱起新的曲调。
sentences.en_text: People report that broadcast music made workmen whistle new tunes.

sentences.cn_text: 一位妇女说，自无线电出现以来，街头打斗减少了,但人们也不再停下来「倚着扫帚柄聊天」了。
sentences.en_text: A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and “talking on the brush handle”.

sentences.cn_text: 总体而言，无线电备受欢迎。
sentences.en_text: By and large the wireless was welcome.

sentences.cn_text: 我喜欢三十年代研究中那位男士的话，他发现无线电突然提供了「丰富多样的内容……一些我原以为自己永远不会感兴趣的东西……或许是冰球之类」。
sentences.en_text: I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered “a lot of variety...things I thought I’d never be interested in...ice hockey perhaps”.

sentences.cn_text: 的确如此：在数字化之前的80多年里，线性语音广播带来了意外之喜，能够随机地为汽车旅程或枯燥的体力活增添生气。
sentences.en_text: True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task.

sentences.cn_text: 在我自己关于广播的书中，我记录了一次驾车经历：「我赶上了新闻，学到了一些17世纪的历史，还被一档朴实无华的听诊器历史节目出乎意料地教育了一番。」
sentences.en_text: In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive: “I caught up with the news, learnt some 17thcentury history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope.”

sentences.cn_text: 但广播那种丰富的意外之喜正在消退。
sentences.en_text: But radio’s enriching serendipity is ebbing.

sentences.cn_text: 随着多个网络和无数播客的涌现，智能手机用户可以选择听什么以及何时听。
sentences.en_text: With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管戴着耳机散步可以听任何内容十分美妙，但无限的选择促使我们退缩到小众兴趣和志趣相投的信念中。
sentences.en_text: And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.

sentences.cn_text: 马可尼和里斯的时代已过去一百年，单纯倾听的艺术是否正面临威胁？
sentences.en_text: A hundred years on from Marconi and Reith, is the art of mere listening endangered?

sentences.cn_text: 有人会说有声书的繁荣让它得以复兴，尽管我想你随后又会担心阅读的衰落。
sentences.en_text: Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading.

sentences.cn_text: 但发明塑造着我们所有人，当技术社会习惯确实发生改变时，值得留意，并思考是否要稍加控制或保护年幼一代。
sentences.en_text: But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest.

sentences.cn_text: 无论我们做什么，创新都会发生。
sentences.en_text: Whatever we do, innovation will happen.

sentences.cn_text: 今天我们为盯着智能手机屏幕和自拍虚荣的孤立文化而忧虑，但早在1939年就有那位女士感慨，当她所在街区家家户户都装上无线电后，邻里间「倚着扫帚柄聊天」的习惯就消失了。
sentences.en_text: Today we fret about the isolating culture of smartphone-staring and selfievanity, but already in 1939 there was that lady regretting how, when all her street got wirelesses, it lost the neighbourly habit of “talking on the brush handle”.

sentences.cn_text: 这足以让人放下智能手机，拿起院子扫帚走到门前。
sentences.en_text: It’s enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.

sentences.cn_text: 从约翰·里斯爵士的话中可以了解到关于无线电的什么信息？
sentences.en_text: What can be learnt about wireless from Sir John Reith?

sentences.cn_text: 它对所有人都是可及的。
sentences.en_text: It was accessible to everyone.

sentences.cn_text: 它改善了人际关系。
sentences.en_text: It improved interpersonal relations.

sentences.cn_text: 它是人类才智的奇迹。
sentences.en_text: It was a miracle of human ingenuity.

sentences.cn_text: 它开启了一个孤立文化的新时代。
sentences.en_text: It led to a new era of isolating culture.

sentences.cn_text: 牛津大学博德利图书馆展览的主题是什么？
sentences.en_text: What is the theme of the exhibition at the Bodleian in Oxford?

sentences.cn_text: 广播对早期受众的影响。
sentences.en_text: The impact of radio on its early audience.

sentences.cn_text: 广播在公共音乐教育中的作用。
sentences.en_text: The role of radio in public music education.

sentences.cn_text: 广播技术的革新过程。
sentences.en_text: The innovation process of radio technology.

sentences.cn_text: 广播领域的杰出先驱。
sentences.en_text: The eminent pioneers in radio broadcasting.

sentences.cn_text: 关于广播的研究过去并不充分。
sentences.en_text: the research on radio used to be inadequate.

sentences.cn_text: 广播的魅力在数字时代依然存在。
sentences.en_text: the charm of radio remains in the digital age.

sentences.cn_text: 广播听众可能获得意外收获。
sentences.en_text: radio listeners could make unexpected gains.

sentences.cn_text: 多年来广播节目变化甚微。
sentences.en_text: radio shows have changed little over the years.

sentences.cn_text: 第3段和第6段中的表达「倚着扫帚柄聊天」指的是 ____ 的行为。
sentences.en_text: The expression “talking on the brush handle” in Paragraphs 3 and 6 refers to the act of ____

sentences.cn_text: 制造很大的噪音。
sentences.en_text: making a loud noise.

sentences.cn_text: 随意闲聊。
sentences.en_text: having a casual chat.

sentences.cn_text: 引发一场无关紧要的争吵。
sentences.en_text: starting a trivial quarrel.

sentences.cn_text: 哼唱一首流行歌曲。
sentences.en_text: humming a popular song.

sentences.cn_text: 在最后一段，作者意在表达的观点是 ____
sentences.en_text: In the last paragraph, the author intends to express the opinion that ____

sentences.cn_text: 技术应以造福人类为目标。
sentences.en_text: technology should be aimed at benefiting humans.

sentences.cn_text: 应该采取行动复兴倾听的艺术。
sentences.en_text: actions should be taken to revive the art of listening.

sentences.cn_text: 青少年应养成健康的社交媒体习惯。
sentences.en_text: adolescents should form healthy social media habits.

sentences.cn_text: 人们应对创新持理性态度。
sentences.en_text: people should adopt a sensible attitude to innovations.
